summary: The two rewritten units are now sound. In capacity-and-best-interests the MCA 2005 rules are stated correctly: s25(2)(b) (a later LPA covering the same treatment invalidates an earlier advance decision, a later advance decision or a silent LPA does not), the s11(7)(c) express-authority rule for life-sustaining treatment, and the s25(5)-(6) formalities including the 'even if life is at risk' statement. The worked example, key point and q004/q006/q010 keys are internally consistent and the dated stems work out (the example's 'November 2026' matches the current date). In triage-and-scarcity the P1/P2/P3 flow, the dead (white) label, the worked-example answers and all numeric keys (0.75, 1.8, 12, 8 vs 4) check out. No critical or major issues were found. Remaining issues are minor: an unverified sieve version, garbled characters in the reproductive unit, a stale assisted-dying status note, a morphine example in renal impairment, and several round-2 minors left unchanged. This is an AI review only: the course still needs a subject-matter expert in medical law, ethics and clinical practice before clinical or professional reliance, and the sieve thresholds, assisted-dying and abortion-law status, and GMP 2024 domain mapping are unverified and need a source check.

issues.problem: The 'illustrative sieve card' (respiratory rate below 10 or above 29, pulse above 120, capillary refill over 2 s) is described throughout as 'the UK sieve' ('The sieve taught here is the UK sieve'; q001-q003 'Using the UK triage sieve'). The step order (walk, then airway opened and not breathing = dead, breathing only after airway opening = P1, then rate, then circulation) matches UK practice, and dead (white) is the correct UK label. The numeric cut-offs are those of older MIMMS-style cards; I believe more recent NARU/JESIP-aligned cards use different physiological thresholds (unverified). The card also has no catastrophic-haemorrhage step although the table lists 'severe external bleeding' as a P1 example.
issues.suggestedFix: Source-check against the current NARU/JESIP/MIMMS sieve. Either cite the version and date of the card, or word the lesson as 'a UK-style sieve with illustrative cut-offs' instead of 'the UK sieve'. Note the catastrophic-haemorrhage step or drop 'severe external bleeding' from the P1 example. The existing 'always use your own service's card' caveat is good and should stay.

issues.problem: The lesson says 'in every question the thresholds will be given in the stem', but q001, q002 and q003 give none. q003 option a refers to 'the card limits' without stating them. The key (P1) is right and does not depend on them.
issues.suggestedFix: State the thresholds in the q003 stem, or change the lesson sentence to 'where thresholds matter, they will be given in the stem'.

issues.problem: The text and table cite 's11(7)(c)' for the express-authority rule on life-sustaining treatment. This matches common citation of the Act and Code of Practice (with the express-provision requirement in s11(8)). I could not verify the exact subsection from here.
issues.suggestedFix: Check the section numbers against legislation.gov.uk. If needed, cite 's11(7)(c) and (8)'. The substance of the rule is correct.

issues.problem: In the paediatric context the marking guide gives 'Refusal: a decision not to proceed; if the person has capacity, refusal should be respected', and the lesson table says refusal 'must be respected if the person has capacity'. In England and Wales a competent child's refusal can in some circumstances be overridden by a person with parental responsibility or the court (for example Re W), which a student could miss.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a marking point and a lesson line: a competent child's refusal carries great weight but is not binding in the way an adult's is. Overriding it requires parental or court authority and is a last resort.

issues.problem: Corrupted characters in the key option: 'cannot be pers귭 to tell parents'. The same fault appears in the q003 (assisted-reproduction unit) explanation: 'at least one s쳮ds'.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace with 'cannot be persuaded to tell their parents or allow the clinician to do so' and 'at least one succeeds'. Scan the course for other non-ASCII corruption.

issues.problem: Unchanged from round 2. Table ground F merges the two statutory emergency grounds (F: immediate termination to save life; G: immediate termination to prevent grave permanent injury). Summary and q009 say 'A, B, E and F' have no fixed limit, which omits G.
issues.suggestedFix: Split into F and G, or state that F is a simplification. Update the summary and q009 marking guide to include G.

issues.problem: The course is framed as UK, England and Wales, but the unit is written for 'Great Britain', and its worked example and q005 rest on the Scottish statutory test (Age of Legal Capacity (Scotland) Act 1991). The England and Wales route (Gillick and Fraser) gets only the definition and q006. The unit also does not state that abortion law in England and Wales has recently been the subject of decriminalisation legislation. I have not verified the current status; please check.
issues.suggestedFix: Lead with the England and Wales position, keep Scotland as a short comparison, and source-check the current abortion-law position before use.

issues.problem: Lesson and q006 state flatly that donor-conceived people 'can obtain identifying information about the donor at 18'. This applies to donations from April 2005 onward (earlier donors were anonymous unless they have registered), and non-identifying information can be requested from 16.
issues.suggestedFix: Add 'for donations made after 1 April 2005' and mention the age-16 non-identifying information right.

issues.problem: The 'Police request after a violent injury' example concerns a stab wound and concludes that, with no legal basis, the clinician should 'refuse the broader request'. It omits the GMC expectation that police are told promptly when a person arrives with a knife or gunshot wound, with identifying details disclosed only if justified. The lesson text only hints at this ('local legal duties or policy').
issues.suggestedFix: Add that GMC guidance expects prompt notification to police of knife and gunshot wounds, limited to the fact and nature of the injury unless identification is justified. Keep the advice to seek senior or Caldicott input for a request for further detail such as the alcohol level or what the patient said.

issues.problem: The marking guide says 'the relevant authority notified through the proper route'. For known FGM in a girl under 18, regulated professionals must report to the police (non-emergency 101), normally within one month, alongside a safeguarding referral. The guide does not say this.
issues.suggestedFix: Add: report to the police under the mandatory duty (FGM Act 2003 s5B), plus a safeguarding referral and senior advice.

issues.problem: q007 asks about principles 'in UK GDPR', but the lesson never names UK GDPR or the Data Protection Act 2018. It says only 'data protection legislation' and 'Seven data protection principles'. The question is a counting item that tests recall of the number, not understanding.
issues.suggestedFix: Name UK GDPR and the DPA 2018 in the lesson, and replace q007 with an item that applies a principle.

issues.problem: The worked example (reduced renal function) and table suggest 'a regular oral opioid such as morphine'. Morphine metabolites accumulate in renal impairment and it is usually avoided or dose-reduced, with alternatives such as oxycodone preferred on specialist or local guidance. The text does say to check renal function and follow local policy, but the named example points the wrong way.
issues.suggestedFix: Say 'an opioid chosen and dosed for renal function (morphine is usually avoided or reduced in renal impairment; alternatives are used per local palliative guidance)', or use an example patient with normal renal function.

issues.problem: The ACP worked example records a wish to avoid invasive ventilation and q009 asks what should be recorded, but neither says that an ACP statement is not legally binding. A binding refusal needs a valid advance decision (MCA ss24-26, the other unit). q004 and q008 are subtraction and percentage filler (8 minus 5; 9 to 6) unrelated to the objectives.
issues.suggestedFix: Add that an ACP records preferences, while a refusal of specified treatment must be an ADRT to bind. Replace q004 and q008 with questions on symptom management or ACP.

issues.problem: Unchanged from round 2. The status note says the lesson reflects 'current parliamentary debate as at June 2024', which is stale (the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill was introduced later, in the 2024-25 session). The current status of that Bill and any Scottish bill is unverified here, so q010 and the summary line 'assisting suicide remains an offence' should be checked. The math block still contains literal '\\[ ... \\]' delimiters inside a cases environment, which may not render.
issues.suggestedFix: Check the live Parliament record and update or remove the dated claim. Remove the redundant delimiters from the latex.

issues.problem: The consultee worked example and q006 (an adult lacking capacity in a non-CTIMP study) omit the MCA ss30-33 conditions: the research must be connected with an impairing condition or its treatment, and it cannot be done as effectively with capacitous participants. A student could assume any incapacitated adult can be enrolled via a consultee. Unchanged from round 2: q007 asks how many 'core elements' are listed (capacity, information, voluntariness, signed form) and tests counting.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the s31 conditions to the lesson and the marking guidance. Replace q007 with 'which of these is evidence of consent rather than a core element'.

issues.problem: The math block shows a percentage-affected formula (with literal '\\[ ... \\]' delimiters) that no worked example or question uses. It is unrelated to the objectives.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the block or replace it with a decision aid (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, conflict of interest).

issues.problem: The statutory duty of candour is described only for England. Since April 2023 Wales has its own organisational duty under the Health and Social Care (Quality and Engagement) (Wales) Act 2020, and the course is framed as England and Wales. The mislabelled-sample worked example (one extra day) is also unlikely to reach the statutory 'moderate harm' threshold, but the unit does not make clear that the professional duty applies regardless.
issues.suggestedFix: Add one line on the Welsh duty (verify details) and note that the professional duty applies at any level of harm.

issues.problem: Unchanged from round 2. q005 (09:14 to 09:31) and q009 (16:22 to 16:37) are time-subtraction filler unrelated to the objectives and near-duplicates. The math block (delta t) is also unused.
issues.suggestedFix: Delete or replace with application questions on escalation routes or protected disclosure (ERA 1996 Part IVA).

issues.problem: Unchanged from round 2. q003 and q006 repeat the lesson worked-example numbers exactly (24 vs 12 per 1,000; 48 vs 12 per 100,000), so the answer is in the lesson. The maternal-mortality figures are presented as 'a maternal mortality review' and give a rate ratio of 4.0, whereas recent MBRRACE-UK figures for Black women are roughly three times those for White women (unverified, source check), so students may recall the invented figure as fact.
issues.suggestedFix: Label the figures as illustrative, use different figures in the questions, and add one more gender or ethnicity example.

issues.problem: Unchanged from round 2. The math block lists fitness-to-practise concern as 'conduct, competence, health, character'. 'Character' is not a GMC ground; impairment arises from misconduct, deficient professional performance, adverse physical or mental health, a conviction or caution, another body's determination, or inadequate English. q004 (18/24) and q007 (9/30) are trivial percentage filler, and q006 repeats the lesson's visual-impairment worked example almost verbatim. q008 (looking up a celebrity's record) keys 'Trust and professionalism'; confidentiality may also sit under 'Patients, partnership and communication' in GMP 2024 (unverified), so the key may be contestable.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the GMC impairment categories. Replace q004/q007 with substantive items on process or domains. Rewrite q006 with a new scenario. Check the GMP 2024 paragraph for confidentiality and either cite it in the explanation or reword q008 so only one domain fits.
